skill.name: file-path-traversal
skill.description: Guide authorized security teams through path traversal testing, impact assessment, and remediation for web application file access issues.
skill.summary: Test directory traversal exposure and document safe remediation.
skill.author: zebbern

security_audit.summary: The skill is explicitly offensive and includes payloads for sensitive file disclosure, SSH key targeting, SAM hive access, and LFI-to-RCE escalation. Markdown backtick detections are false positives, but most filesystem, sensitive file, network exploit, and blocker findings are confirmed.

remediation.issue: Sensitive file exfiltration targets are included as routine payloads.
remediation.suggestion: Remove targets such as password files, SSH keys, SAM hives, and process environment files. Use safe canary files for validation.

remediation.issue: The skill teaches LFI-to-RCE escalation through log poisoning and PHP wrappers.
remediation.suggestion: Remove command execution workflows and replace them with defensive explanations and lab-only references.

remediation.issue: Automated fuzzing commands can be used against systems outside scope.
remediation.suggestion: Add stronger scope checks, rate limits, authorization requirements, and safe evidence handling before any automation.

remediation.issue: Remediation guidance is present but outweighed by exploit-focused workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Refocus the skill on detection planning, secure coding patterns, and sanitized proof collection.

content.value_statement: Path traversal bugs can expose server files and credentials. This skill guides authorized testers through discovery, validation, impact assessment, and remediation.
actual_capabilities: Explains path traversal concepts, impact, and common vulnerable file parameters.
Provides authorized testing workflows for traversal, encoding, and validation bypass checks.
Lists Linux, Windows, web server, and application file targets for impact analysis.
Covers Burp Suite, ffuf, and wfuzz workflows for controlled fuzzing.
Describes LFI escalation paths that require strict authorization and containment.
Includes prevention patterns for PHP and Python file access logic.
limitations: Requires written authorization and a clearly defined testing scope.
Examples use placeholder targets and must be adapted carefully.
Unsafe use can expose secrets or disrupt production systems.
Does not replace full secure code review or remediation validation.

use_cases.title: Validate Download Endpoints
use_cases.description: Test whether file download or viewer parameters can escape the intended directory.

use_cases.title: Prepare Remediation Tickets
use_cases.description: Convert confirmed traversal behavior into clear impact, evidence, and fix guidance.

use_cases.title: Review File Access Logic
use_cases.description: Compare application file handling against canonical path validation and allowlist patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how path traversal could affect this authorized staging feature. Focus on safe validation and remediation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Test Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a path traversal test plan for this in-scope endpoint. Include prerequisites, evidence handling, and stop conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these authorized test results and classify impact. Redact sensitive data and recommend fixes for each affected parameter.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Controlled Escalation
prompt_templates.prompt: For an approved lab, outline when LFI may become code execution. Include approvals, containment, and safe evidence collection.

output_examples.input: An authorized staging endpoint accepts a file parameter for downloads.
output: Assessment plan with scope, safe test cases, and stop conditions.
Evidence checklist that avoids collecting private keys or password hashes.
Remediation advice using allowlists and canonical path checks.

output_examples.input: A developer needs to fix unsafe file access in a web handler.
output: Root cause summary for unsanitized path construction.
Recommended validation strategy using canonical paths and approved filenames.
Regression test ideas for traversal, encoding, and absolute path inputs.

output_examples.input: An AppSec lead needs report language for confirmed traversal exposure.
output: Business impact summary with sensitive data redacted.
Severity rationale based on reachable files and application context.
Concrete remediation steps and verification criteria.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization and scope before running any test.
Use canary files or lab fixtures before attempting sensitive paths.
Redact secrets and pair every finding with remediation guidance.
anti_patterns: Running traversal payloads against systems outside the approved scope.
Collecting private keys, password hashes, or tokens as proof.
Treating a blocked payload as proof that the code is safe.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Security testers, AppSec engineers, and developers working on authorized web application assessments.

faq.question: Does this skill require authorization?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it only with written permission and a clear scope.

faq.question: Can it help with remediation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes allowlist, canonical path, and safe file access guidance.

faq.question: Does it collect secrets automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill is guidance only, but unsafe prompts can lead to sensitive data exposure.

faq.question: Which tools does it mention?
faq.answer: It references browser developer tools, Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP, cURL, ffuf, and wfuzz.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production testing?
faq.answer: Only with explicit approval, careful rate limits, and evidence handling rules.
